feat(ui): implement proper edge-to-edge support (Android 15 / targetSdk 35) (#357)

* feat(ui): implement proper edge-to-edge support (Android 15 / targetSdk 35)

Enable and refine full edge-to-edge rendering across the app in line with
Android 15 behavior (targetSdk >= 35). Ensures immersive layouts while
preserving correct system bar insets and visual consistency.

Changes:
- Synchronized light/dark system bar appearance with LissenTheme
- Removed hardcoded Modifier.systemBarsPadding() from Scaffolds to allow
  backgrounds to render edge-to-edge
- Applied correct insets handling within LazyColumn content to prevent
  overlap with status and navigation bars (e.g., LibraryScreen)
- Updated custom bottom components (MiniPlayer, NavigationBar) to use
  proper navigationBarsPadding() instead of fixed height constraints
- Adjusted PullRefreshIndicator positioning to avoid overlap with
  translucent TopAppBars

All screens verified for correct inset handling and immersive scroll behavior.

Closes #356

fix: use relative URLs in Retrofit API client for subpath compatibility (#379)

When Audiobookshelf is hosted behind a reverse proxy at a subpath
(e.g., https://example.com/audiobookshelf/), Retrofit endpoints with
leading slashes (like /api/libraries) resolve against the domain root,
discarding the base URL path. This causes all API calls to 404.

Remove leading slashes from all endpoint annotations so Retrofit
correctly appends them to the full base URL including any subpath.

Fix Android Auto seek buttons doing nothing for car-initiated playback (#466)

Two issues prevented the head unit seek controls from working:

1. Books started from the Android Auto browse screen never populated
   MediaRepository's playingBook state, which is only set by the phone
   UI flow. Since rewind/forward/previousTrack/nextTrack all bail out
   silently on a null playingBook, every seek button on the head unit
   was a no-op while pause kept working (it bypasses MediaRepository).
   onSetMediaItems now registers the fetched book with MediaRepository.

2. The rewind/forward buttons were assigned to SLOT_OVERFLOW, leaving
   the primary back/forward slots to chapter navigation. Swapped so the
   configurable rewind/forward occupy the primary slots, matching
   audiobook app conventions, with chapter navigation in the overflow.

arriving via logcat and seeks now applied for books started from the
car screen.

into a first-class safeCacheableApiCall that takes the cached object and
returns a CacheableResult (Fresh / NotModified / Error). Both safeApiCall

refactor: generalize the user state provider into a shared ConditionalCache

Replace the single-endpoint UserStateProvider with a generic in-memory
ConditionalCache: a map of per-key entries (mutex + value + etag). An
endpoint becomes revalidate-on-read by routing it through load(key) {
client, etag -> ... }, with no per-endpoint cache class. /api/me is the
first key; logout/login drop the whole cache via invalidateAll().

refactor: fold conditional caching into a single safeApiCall facade

Developers now call one makeRequest for every endpoint and opt a call into
ETag revalidation by tagging the Retrofit method with @Tag Cacheable, instead
of picking a cache-specific method or threading If-None-Match through
signatures. A ConditionalCacheInterceptor adds If-None-Match from a URL-keyed
store and safeApiCall serves the cached object on 304 or stores body+ETag on
200.

feat: bound the conditional cache with a weighted LRU and a refetch fallback

The URL-keyed store grew without limit, which was fine while only /api/me was
tagged but would leak memory once large or paginated GETs opt in. Entries now
carry a weight (element count) and the store evicts least-recently-used ones to
stay under a budget; reads keep an entry hot.

Two edges follow from bounding: a 200 without an ETag is no longer cached, since
a body with no validator can never answer a 304; and a 304 whose object was
evicted between the interceptor sending the validator and us reading it back is
transparently re-issued to the network instead of failing.

feat: opt rarely-changing library GETs into conditional caching

Tag the metadata and listing endpoints (libraries, library detail, paginated
library/podcast items, authors, item and episode detail) with @Tag Cacheable so
their bodies are revalidated with If-None-Match and served from the LRU on 304.

Left untagged on purpose: POST/DELETE writes, search (low hit rate, wants fresh
results), the personalized feed and per-item progress (they change constantly, so
revalidation never matches and they would only churn the bounded cache), and the
streaming cover/author images, whose ResponseBody cannot be replayed from cache.

Caching still self-selects at runtime: an entry is only stored when the server
returns an ETag, so endpoints that do not support it stay a no-op.

perf: measure cache weight by reflective element count

toString().length scaled linearly with the payload and allocated ~8x its
size on every cache write (measured: 3.6ms / 16MB for a 10k-item page),
which is pure garbage on the hot userState path. Sum the element counts of
top-level collections instead: O(1) and ~30 bytes per call, same eviction
behavior since each response wraps one list. The collection-field set is
resolved once per class and cached; setAccessible is guarded so JDK-internal
values (e.g. String's byte[]) are skipped instead of throwing.

Also fix the Cacheable KDoc to show the defaulted @Tag parameter.

refactor: back ConditionalCache with androidx.collection.LruCache

Replace the hand-rolled LinkedHashMap/totalWeight/evictToBudget with the
maintained weighted LRU that was already on the classpath. The weight is
computed once on write and frozen onto the entry, so LruCache's accounting
never re-measures a value that could mutate; etag/value/invalidate/invalidateAll
map onto get/remove/evictAll and the internal synchronization lets the
@Synchronized annotations go.
